title: John Dillinger — the jailbreak with a gun that may have been carved from wood
sources: Wikipedia: John Dillinger — accused of robbing 24 banks; captured in Tucson in January 1934 and held at the Lake County jail in Crown Point, Indiana, which local police boasted was escape-proof, with extra guards; on 3 March 1934 he escaped during morning exercises, producing a pistol and taking hostages without firing a shot; whether the gun was real is disputed — Deputy Ernest Blunk said it was real, FBI files say it was carved from wood, the trustee Sam Cahoon believed he carved it with a razor from shelving in his cell, and the lawyer's investigator Art O'Leary claimed he smuggled the gun in himself; he had plastic surgery in 1934; Ana Cumpănaș (Anna Sage) tipped off the Bureau to avoid deportation; on 22 July 1934 he was shot dead by agents in an alley beside the Biograph Theater, Chicago, after watching Manhattan Melodrama; souvenir hunters dipped handkerchiefs in his blood.
FBI wanted poster (1934): wanted under the National Motor Vehicle Theft Act for taking the car of Lillian Holley, Sheriff of Lake County, from Crown Point to Chicago.

Photos (public domain, Wikimedia Commons / FBI / Library of Congress): Dillinger's mug shots (1924, 1934); the 1934 FBI wanted poster; the Lake County Sheriff's House and Jail, Crown Point; evidence from his hideout (1934); Anna Sage (1934); Melvin Purvis; the Biograph Theater in 1934 and the crowd after his death
Archive film (public domain): 'Depression era gangsters' newsreel; 'Saint Paul Police Detectives and Their Work' (1941) — illustrative
Music: Margie (1920), Gene Rodemich's Orchestra, 1921 recording, public domain

In 1934, the most wanted man in America broke out of an "escape-proof" jail — with a gun he may have carved out of wood.

John Dillinger, accused of robbing 24 banks, was locked up in the Lake County jail in Crown Point, Indiana. Police told the papers it was escape-proof and posted extra guards. On 3 March 1934, during morning exercise, Dillinger pulled out a pistol, took hostages, locked up the guards and walked out without firing a shot — then drove away in the sheriff's own car.

Was the gun real? FBI files say he carved it from wood with a razor blade. A deputy swore it was real. His lawyer's investigator claimed he smuggled it in himself. Nobody agrees to this day.

The stolen car crossing a state line made him a federal case. Four months later, tipped off by Anna Sage, agents shot him dead outside the Biograph Theater in Chicago.

youtube.description:
In 1934, the most wanted man in America broke out of an escape-proof jail — with a gun he may have carved out of wood.

On 3 March 1934, bank robber John Dillinger pulled a pistol during morning exercise at the Lake County jail in Crown Point, Indiana, took hostages, locked up the guards and drove off in the sheriff's own car without firing a shot. FBI files say the gun was carved from wood; a deputy swore it was real; his lawyer's investigator claimed he smuggled it in. Driving the stolen car across a state line made him a federal case, and J. Edgar Hoover's agents hunted him as Public Enemy No. 1 — until he was shot dead outside the Biograph Theater in Chicago on 22 July 1934.
